$anchorDrift: Gated at 0 from the day it shipped, because `--accept` IS the escape hatch: a legitimate anchor change is accepted by typing its id, which is exactly the intended cost. An exception is pinned to a siteKey, so an anchor that moved silently stops excusing anything — this is the check that says so out loud.
$comment: Every number here is a floor somebody raised deliberately. Lowering one needs a commit message that says why. The `hard` entries are not per-case negotiable: they are the claims the product makes.
$catalog: The ratchet. `checkCatalog` validates a rule's SHAPE — docs present, reason present — and never its REACHABILITY, so a rule can be well-formed, cited, and unable to fire in any repository. The runner fails when a rule outside the allowlist goes unexercised (a new dead rule), and fails when a listed one starts firing (the list is stale). It may only shrink.
$neverExercisedWhy: Empty, and it stays empty by ratchet. Four rules used to sit here because they were well-formed, cited, and unable to fire: the two TOML ones had no extractor, `docker.label` matched a key the prose reader never produced, and `html.title` described a shape the HTML extractor does not emit. Three got a reader; the fourth got a rule matching what was always there. A fifth dead rule fails the run, and so does a listed one that starts firing.
